newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Clabecq workers delay action,await ruling.
newsitem.headline: Clabecq workers delay action,await ruling.

text.p: Workers at Forges de Clabecq SA decided on Friday to postpone any action to try and safeguard their jobs until a court ruling on the future on the loss-making Belgian steel firm, union sources said.
Workers had planned to march on Friday on the southern city of Namur, the seat of the Walloon regional government which is the majority shareholder in Clabecq.
A rally in Brussels, the seat of the European Union, had also been scheduled.
A Belgian commercial court is to rule on the viability of the troubled firm on January 3 after receiving a report from a court-appointed receiver.
"If on Friday January 3 the commercial court decides on bankruptcy, the unions will call a general assembly for January 4," a union source said after a meeting of workers on Friday.
"If the court decides on a resumption of work we will take the time to examine the situation." In any case there would be a march for jobs at Clabecq on February 2, he said.
Clabecq filed for bankruptcy last Thursday after the Walloon region withdrew its support.

The fate of the company, which employs nearly 1,800 people, appeared to have been sealed on the Wednesday before when the European Commission rejected a 1.5 billion Belgian franc rescue plan by Wallonia for Clabecq.
The Commission said the subsidies went against European Union rules which only allow steel sector aid for environmental reasons, for research and development or for company closure.

Clabecq had been struggling to survive in a heavily cyclical industry marked by overcapacity and cheap imports from eastern Europe and had failed to find a partner to improve its competitive position.

On December 24 the court ruled against declaring Clabecq bankrupt after two experts said the company was still viable. The experts said Clabecq could survive in its current form until mid-1997 in view of its order book. Its activities should be reduced and a restructuring considered thereafter.
The court appointed a company receiver to draw up a financial plan based on a full resumption of work from January 6 and start-up of the furnace from January 4.
Clabecq shares were last quoted at 76 francs on December 19.

Bid and ask prices are indicated at 12 francs but the actual decline is limited by a bourse rule capping the maximum movement in the share at 10 percent above or below the previous day's closing price.
The share recorded its 1996 high on January 5 when it stood at 476 francs.
